short: Public boundary: the AT Protocol adapter (OAuth, PDS, did:plc)
is: The public data boundary: the only crate that knows the AT Protocol — OAuth sign-in, PDS record/blob writes, public profile reads, and real did:plc minting with key custody — quarantining jacquard behind domain port traits.
conventions: Nothing protocol-shaped leaks past this crate's surface (the jacquard client type is a private alias).
Uses `PgPool` as a plain DB client injected by `composition`; its queries run against adapter-pg's migrations.
OAuth at-rest secrets (DPoP key, tokens, PKCE verifier) are envelope-encrypted under the same custody root key as adapter-pg's `key_vault`.
`auth_store` is one of the five documented Unit-of-Work exemptions.
Genesis signatures are atproto-canonical ECDSA-SHA256 low-S via atrium-crypto — never hand-rolled.

Every fetch to a host a visitor, a handle or a DID document names goes through `guarded_http::GuardedHttp`; only `guarded_http/client.rs`, `plc_directory.rs` and `public_records.rs` (operator-configured hosts) may name reqwest, only this crate's manifest may list it (never renamed), and `tests/network_door.rs` fails the build otherwise — it also forbids jacquard's bare-reqwest sessions and resolvers, the named transport-weakening calls (TLS, proxy, address pinning, any redirect policy but `Policy::none()`), and any caller of `AtprotoPublicRecords` outside its own file and the façade, until its transport is settled with the hosted-repos design decision (endpoint from operator config only).

refs.title: Libraries as Composition — the Approved Crate Set and the Newtype Derive Rules
refs.governs: dev-deps proptest (PLC signing determinism), wiremock (directory/PDS/guarded-client mocks) and tokio-rustls (an untrusted-certificate TLS server for the guarded client); hickory-resolver 0.26 as the guarded client's DNS client (supplies DNS, dictates nothing); jacquard with default features off (no hickory 0.24)

notes: Port → impl: `Authenticator` = `AtprotoAuthenticator` (lib.rs) · `ProfileSource` = `AtprotoProfileSource` · `DidMinter` = `RealDidMinter` / `StubDidMinter` · `PublicRecords` = `AtprotoPublicRecords`. `PlcDirectory` is adapter-local, selected by `plc_directory_from_config`.

`secret_vault::SecretVault` deliberately mirrors adapter-pg's `key_vault::RootKey` (same AEAD, blob format and root key `ZURFUR_DID_KEY_ROOT_KEY`) rather than sharing a type — one adapter may not depend on another. Hoisting the envelope into `domain` is the open follow-up. Root-key custody is DEV-ONLY (config/env) pending a KMS; `composition::ensure_custody_hardened` covers this store too at boot.
Op ordering: `mint` writes custody + the genesis op BEFORE submitting; `tombstone` and `update_handle` submit BEFORE recording, so a failed submit never advances the local chain.
`plc.rs` is pinned to the published vector `did:plc:ewvi7nxzyoun6zhxrhs64oiz`; it is the tripwire for the whole DAG-CBOR → sha256 → base32/24 pipeline.
This crate's half of the `codegen_current` staleness gate lives over in adapter-pg's `tests/it/`, not here.

Guarded web client (`src/guarded_http/`): `policy.rs` = `PublicHttpsUrl` (https, port 443, no userinfo, a domain host of 2+ labels outside the local/reserved TLDs; IP literals refused in every spelling); `address.rs` = the address table (`PublicAddress`: IPv4 deny-list, IPv6 allow-list `2000::/3` with mapped/NAT64 unwrapped); `dns.rs` = `FilteringDns` (fully qualified lookups, 5 s outer timeout, any forbidden answer refuses the name) over one hickory `SystemDns`; `client.rs` = `GuardedHttp` (reqwest 0.12 with the filter as its resolver, no redirects, https-only, no proxy, no decompression, 10 s total timeout, 512 KiB cap with crate-private `send_capped`). Errors split into `Refused` / `NotFound` / `Unavailable` (`errors.rs`). Design record: `.understand/20261008-hardened-resolver-design.md`.

Interim (until the identity resolver replaces them): the OAuth client is `OAuthClient::new_from_resolver(JacquardResolver<GuardedHttp>)` and the profile source an `Agent` over the same, both still on jacquard's default `ResolverOptions` (Bluesky handle fallback included). Dev and production share the strict policy, so a plain-http or local PDS is unreachable.

Test seam, `#[cfg(test)]` only (never a feature): `GuardedHttp::relaxed` (loopback, http, any port), `GuardedHttp::scripted` (strict policy over `guarded_http/scripted.rs`'s scripted DNS), `GuardedHttp::upstream` (strict policy and DNS filter, then plaintext to a mock with `Host` kept).
